Acumen

AK-yuh-mun -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, AK. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Acumen is ability to make good judgments.

Admirals praised the young captain's tactical acumen during the storm rescue.

Worked Example

The student council treasurer reads the fundraiser proposal twice, then circles one line: the vendor's 'free' popcorn machine requires buying their overpriced kernels for a year. The council votes it down and saves half its budget.

The treasurer showed acumen: the ability to make good, sharp judgments. Notice how the word usually travels with a modifier that names the arena -- business acumen, political acumen, financial acumen -- because acumen is sharpness applied to a particular field.

How Acumen Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

insight

insight: the ability to see the true nature of a situation

judgment

judgment: the ability to make sensible decisions

sharpness

sharpness: quickness and precision of mind

Antonyms

foolishness

foolishness: a lack of good sense

dullness

dullness: slowness of mind

How Strong Is It? — insight → judgment → acumen

insight vs. acumen

insight vs. acumen: Insight is a flash of seeing one situation clearly, while acumen is the standing equipment -- the practiced sharpness that produces good judgment case after case.

judgment vs. acumen

judgment vs. acumen: Judgment is the strongest match: both name the power to decide well, but acumen adds a blade's edge -- judgment that is not just sound but quick, sharp, and hard to fool.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — acu-

root — acu-: sharp, a point, a needle (Latin acuere 'to sharpen')

suffix — -men

suffix — -men: result or means of an action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Acumen is Latin for 'a sharpened point' -- the tip of a needle or spear, from acuere, 'to sharpen.' English kept the metaphor and dropped the hardware: acumen is a sharpened mind, judgment honed to a point that cuts straight through bad deals and weak arguments.

Use the root in a new word: acupuncture

Use the root in a new word: acupuncture: The clinic offers acupuncture, treating patients with fine needles placed at precise points.

Root Check

Word Choice

Acumen almost always follows a modifier naming its arena: business acumen, political acumen, financial acumen, strategic acumen. It is a mass noun -- no one has 'an acumen' or 'three acumens' -- and it praises judgment proven over time, not a single lucky guess.
